side_a: CC 3.1.3.1 "The horizon is the row's own `valid_until`" … "A row without `valid_until` is malformed on this family."
side_b: CC 2.1 "If set, consumer policy treats the attestation as stale after that point, independent of the row's own `expires_at`."
note: CC 3.1.3.1 requires `valid_until` on every `session:*` row and makes it the one staleness instant for every reader. CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 list only `session_id` and `claimed_at` as REQUIRED on `session:*` and give `valid_until` as OPTIONAL consumer policy on every row. A door built from the signed-object table admits a claim with no horizon, which a dead node then holds for ever; CC 3.1.3.1 is the home and the table lacks the row.

side_a: CC 3.1.3 "`ranks` (up to three member keys in order)"
side_b: manifests/family_model.json ballot:moderator body {"member": "ranking", "type": "unstated", "presence": "unstated", "in_cddl": false, "cc_ref": "CC 4.5.13"}; CC 8.10 card "Body: `ranking` (text only), `salt`"; choice_item.cddl "? ranking: [1*3 tstr]"
note: The registry row names the ballot's signed member `ranks`; the family model, its CC 8.10 card and the choice item's answer name it `ranking`, citing CC 4.5.13, which uses neither name. Two emitters reading one each sign different members and each door finds the other's ballot empty. The text has one name, so the data is the side to fix (or the row, if the store ships `ranking`).

side_a: CC 3.2 true iff exactly one live owner-binding on `K` exists, from a `user`-role identity that is not itself steward-bound
side_b: CC 3.2 The re-signed row is a second owner-signed row beside the `self` one, never a replacement, and the audience rule of its tier places it.
note: An announced or group-joined node carries two or more live owner-binding rows by one owner. Read by rows, is_steward_bound is false for it and the steward-binding gate refuses it; read by owners it holds. owner_of ('at most one key') supports counting owners; the data fold (family_model ownership fold: test=count=1 over live rows keyed by attested_key_id) counts rows.

side_a: CC 3.3.5: "Subject withdraws; producer must initiate deletion within sla window"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A producer has proven deletion **iff**, before the deadline, the row was **withdrawn, superseded, or hard-deleted**"
note: What is owed by the end of the window: deletion begun (CC 3.3.5) or deletion done (CC 3.3.1 D1, and CC 2.4.1.1 "deletes within it"). A producer that has only started at the deadline conforms to one and is in breach under the other. D1, the reaction data and CC 2.4.1.1 support done.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "has an allow list of only the cohorts it was set up to serve"
side_b: CC 3.3.7: "receives **no** `self` content beyond the two arms below, and **no** `family` content unless the list names it"
note: A server-class node whose grant carries no `cohorts` member: CC 6.1.5.3 gives it only the cohorts it was set up to serve; the class default of CC 3.3.7 (and the later sentence of CC 6.1.5.3) withholds only self and family, so every community and affiliation of its owner replicates onto it. The two give different holdings for the owner's other communities. Near C381 (which asks about agents), not the same point.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json identity:occurrence replication.audience note: "key-plane reach (Plane::KeyRecord cells; the carrier: everyone)"
note: CC 5.4.6 withholds an occurrence whose attester's owner-binding is not announced, and holds an unannounced identity's occurrence with the owner's nodes and the contact alone; the model cell gives the family one audience, everyone. A kernel reading the cell serves an unannounced person's occurrence to strangers.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A `family` Contribution that supersedes the current one may change metadata or drop members and never adds one."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: "A membership change is never a single-signer `supersedes` Contribution, which a rule-1 or rule-2 `withdraws` could retire without the quorum."
note: CC 3.3.4 lets a superseding family Contribution drop members, and a `supersedes` is its attester's act (CC 2.4.1); the same item then says removal is a cosigned `membership:removal` or a resignation, and CC 4.4.3.4.2 and CC 4.4.3.2.3 say no membership change is a `supersedes`. A reader of the first sentence lets one signer remove a member. The rest of the document supports CC 4.4.3.4.2; the model has "typed record supersede only".

note: the table has no row for an accord roster change: the one row said to cover every accord threshold but the fire is a cosigned row with no window, where CC 4.2.6 runs a roster change as signed participations inside W = 72 h (7 d in declared degradation), counted when W closes. side_a: CC 3.2: "So a stalled roster admits **exactly one row kind without that count**: a widening whose only change is the addition of a **founder** seat."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json membership:{stage} attest guard: "when(leaf=widening) (one trust:confers@landed[attested=signer,val:scope=object] else refuse & type(signer,user) else refuse & not type(signer,node) else refuse)"
note: The guard is written for every widening (reach whole, no stalled-and-recovery condition), so as data it refuses any ordinary widening whose signer holds no trust:confers and is not a user key. The text asks this of the one T7 recovery widening only; the change cell beside it carries the condition `widening[stalled&recovery]`, the guard does not. CC 8.10 prints the same guard.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: "The node-authored form stays valid, and the fold below groups both forms by `attested_key_id`."
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json consent:community_trust signer_rule and fold: "reads=own&signer:owner"
note: The text admits two authors of a trace-capture grant, the owner and the node itself, and refuses only a key that was neither. The signer cell is `owner_of_subject` alone (closed), the card's attest row says owner, and the fold reads owner-signed rows only, so a node-authored grant is not counted as consent. The verbs cell also lacks recant, which the text gives the attester.

side_a: CC 3.2: a lapsed window never detaches a running node
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "dur": "charter.attach_window_secs"
note: reactions.json gives trust:{job} leaf accepts a clock 'attach' (dur charter.attach_window_secs, from cosigned_at, by receipt) and a reaction on its close: read verdict 'closed', force must. Read as data this closes an admitted acceptance edge when the window lapses; T4a says the gate runs at the edge's first admission only and T8 (ii) that an expired attach_window_secs never moves Rooted. formal/derivation/reaction_text.tsv cites for this entry the sentence that forbids it. If 'closed' is meant as 'no new edge may attach on that head', the verdict belongs to the attach attempt (a refusal at the door), not to the family's admitted rows.

side_a: CC 3.2: "An owner ends it by a `withdraws` of the acceptance."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: lineage_witness:{stage} attest none admitted founder,owner selfAct true none
note: lineage_witness:{stage} has verbs attest only (cc-table) and one transition, attest, with undo false; the CC 8.10 card shows no way back. The text lets the node's owner end witnessing by withdrawing the acceptance, after which that key's cosignatures stop counting. The lifecycle cell of the same family (code-v61) does allow attester or subject to withdraw, so the data also disagrees with itself.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "A member votes for the Goal by cosigning it, and the row is admitted only when its full scrub set meets the group's protocol at `asserted_at`."
side_b: data manifests/transitions.tsv: goal:{scale} attest none admitted registered selfAct
note: goal:{scale}, approach:{goal_id}, method:{approach_id}:{substrate_rung} and progress_measure:{method_id} have cosign_rule none and one-signer attest, withdraw and supersede for every row. The text makes a group-declared row (authority_id naming the group) a cosigned row, and says its supersedes, withdraws and recants stand only when cosigned under the same protocol. The data has no arm for the group-declared form, so one member could declare or retire a group's Goal.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A time-boxed guest is a widening with `valid_until`, and the seat lapses at that instant."
side_b: data manifests/reactions.json: "member": "expires_at",
note: The only expiry entry for membership:{stage} is the proposal's expires_at; the family_model lifecycle cell reads "expires_at honoured". Nothing in the data lapses a widening at its valid_until, so a time-boxed guest stays seated. The same gap holds for identity:occurrence (CC 4.4.3.4.6 drops an occurrence past valid_until from the self-collective) and for capacity_assurance:reversible_pending (CC 3.1.2: the binding MUST lapse unless resolved within its valid_until): neither has an expiry entry.
